record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: Which distance metric should be used when determining nearest neighbors in instance-based learning?

evidence.quote: Which distance metric should be used?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider instance-based (memory-based) learning, in which a training set $S = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n \subset \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y}$ is stored, and predictions at a query point $x \in \mathcal{X}$ are made from the labels of the $k$ training instances $x_{i_1}, \dots, x_{i_k}$ minimizing $d(x, x_i)$ for some distance function $d : \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. The performance of such a learner (e.g., its generalization error on an unknown data distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y}$) depends critically on the choice of $d$.

Problem. Provide a principled, general theory for selecting the distance metric $d$ used to determine nearest neighbors in instance-based learning. Specifically:

(a) Identify properties of the data distribution $\mathcal{D}$, the feature space $\mathcal{X}$ (which may mix numeric, ordinal, nominal, and structured attributes), and the target $\mathcal{Y}$ that determine when a given distance $d$ (for example, weighted Minkowski $d_p(x,x') = \big(\sum_j w_j |x_j - x'_j|^p\big)^{1/p}$, Mahalanobis $d_A(x,x') = \sqrt{(x-x')^\top A (x-x')}$ with $A \succeq 0$, value-difference metrics for nominal attributes, or learned metrics) is optimal or near-optimal for $k$-nearest-neighbor prediction.

(b) Give an algorithm that, from the training sample $S$ alone, selects or constructs a distance $d$ whose resulting $k$-NN rule attains generalization error close to $\inf_{d \in \mathcal{F}} \mathrm{err}_{\mathcal{D}}(k\text{-NN}_d)$ over a specified family $\mathcal{F}$ of admissible distances, with finite-sample guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to choose the distance metric in nearest-neighbor / instance-based learning is a longstanding open research direction. Many partial answers exist (Mahalanobis metric learning, LMNN, neighborhood components analysis, value-difference metric, deep metric learning, etc.), but no general theory prescribes the optimal metric for arbitrary data, and the problem is still treated as open in the literature on instance-based learning.

status_evidence.title: Distance Metric Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Selecting an appropriate distance metric is fundamental to many learning algorithms... remains an active area of research.
status_evidence.claim: Choice of distance metric for nearest-neighbor learning is an open, actively researched question with only partial solutions.
